params._camera_note: ASI662MM (IMX662, 1920x1080) as of 2026-08-02, replacing the ASI290MM (1936x1096) this file ran on through PAR-1..PAR-6. It is the only camera enumerated on the bench now. EVERY MEASURED NUMBER IN THIS FILE PREDATES THE SWAP and must be re-taken: fs (the 3788 Hz below is the 290's frame rate at 32x32/exp50/bw100 -- the 662 is a different sensor and readout, so this is the loop period and therefore K's units, the delay in FRAMES, and broad_lp all at once), delay, K, and the pixel scale used to convert error units to px. Re-run the bodes before trusting a run.

Supersedes every earlier start_x/start_y and ROI size in this file and in the prose below. The beam walks several px per hour -- re-probe and re-derive once |park| exceeds ~2 px.

pipeline._comment: Send raw frame to watch_steering.jl on port 64730
pipeline._note: decimation must MATCH the 64731 sink below, so the frame and the CoM cross drawn together come from the same iteration. 64 gives ~36 Hz at a 2310 Hz loop -- about what a GR heatmap can redraw.

pipeline._comment: Track a 15x15 window centred on the previous CoM, so the stray reflection never enters the sum.
pipeline._note: Output stays normalized across the whole 64x64 image, NOT the window: the setpoint is still frame centre and the PID gains below are unchanged. With the beam-centred ROI the stray reflection sits INSIDE the frame at ~(10, 28) and carries flux comparable to the beam, so the old whole-frame acquisition phase can settle between the two spots -- init the window on the beam (frame centre) explicitly instead. The reflection is 22 px from the beam, well outside the 15 px window.
pipeline._shutter: ref_cut drops the frames the rolling shutter cuts. The source is chopped and the sensor reads out row by row, so a frame catches the chop's on-window across only some of its rows and the beam comes back with a hard horizontal edge through it. Those frames are not dark and not dim -- the rows that were lit are at full brightness -- so neither `threshold` nor `min_peak` sees them, and their centroid is pulled toward the surviving rows: a systematic error along the shutter axis that beats against the chop instead of averaging out. The test divides this frame's row profile by a learned reference profile of the whole beam and asks whether some rows are lit while others are not: a whole beam gives the same ratio on every row (so the frame's brightness cancels, and a dim beam is not mistaken for a cut one), a cut beam gives two groups. Rejected frames hold the previous centroid rather than emitting one.
pipeline._shutter_tune: 0.5 means the dimmest judged row must stay above half the frame's typical row. Measured on a simulated sigma=2 beam (tests/test_center_of_mass.c): whole beam 1.00, beam dimmed 4x 0.61, any cut through the judged rows 0.00 -- so the separation is wide and the value is not delicate. Lower toward 0.3 only if the source swings in power by more than ~4x. ref_floor (default 0.25) sets which rows get judged and is the real sensitivity knob: lower it to catch shallower cuts at the price of noisier ratios. ref_warmup 200 frames at loop rate is ~60 ms of learning during which the gate is OFF; the bootstrap takes the row-wise max so it learns the uncut profile even though the chop is already running while it does. STILL WORTH CHECKING that the beam sits well above threshold 10: the threshold subtraction is the one part of this that is not exactly scale-free, and a beam only a few counts over it will tilt the ratios.
pipeline._shutter_cost: Watch the held fraction in the exit summary ("held N of M frames"). A held frame hands the pid the previous frame's error a second time and the integrator keeps winding on it, which reads downstream as added loop delay and eats phase margin. A few percent is fine. If it runs to tens of percent the answer is to stop MAKING partial frames (expose over a whole chop period, or trigger the camera off the chop) rather than to filter them, because by then the loop is running on a small fraction of its nominal rate.

pipeline._comment: Send [y, x] CoM vector to watch_steering.jl on port 64731
pipeline._note: keep decimation equal to the 64730 sink above

pipeline._comment: Send [y, x] CoM vector to watch_error_ts.jl on port 64732
pipeline._note: NOT decimated: this is a time series, and dropping samples without an anti-alias filter folds high-frequency error back down into the band you're trying to read. The packets are ~48 bytes, so full rate is ~110 kB/s -- cheap.

start_delay must be >= the piplate start_delay below. Holding the fine DAC channels without also holding the pid is useless: the integrator keeps winding on the large startup error behind the parked output, and the fine channel is at its rail the instant the hold expires. Base params are the x axis (element 1), *y the y axis (element 0). i sets the crossover: f_c = i*|P|/2pi. Lead-compensated design 2026-07-14 evening (plant from the fine bodes @ bias 2.52/1.62: Kx=0.427, Ky=0.300, tau_loop=1.81 ms; grid search over the attenuation9 open PSD with PM>=45, Ms<=2.0): C(s) = i/s * (s+2pi*8)/(s+2pi*32) on both axes -- the lead's +37 deg buys fc 46->64 Hz (x) / 24->65 Hz (y) at PM 67, paid with 4x less gain below 8 Hz (affordable: 0-10 Hz closed was 0.05 px). Oscillator phases are plant+sensitivity WITH the lead in L: phi = -360*f*tau + angle(1/(1+L)); RECOMPUTE if i/iy/lead/bias change (attenuation8 lesson, validated by attenuation9: x 0.400->0.282 px). Line centers on multi-run measured positions (wander ~0.5 Hz/run); y 11.3 oscillator added (0.095 px line, steady across runs). Rollback = attenuation9 tune: i=680/iy=500, no lead, see attenuation_test.json _note4. Full rationale there.
PARPORT DAC. TWO channels only -- there is no coarse stage: ch0 = y/tip (DACA), ch1 = x/tilt (DACB). Here y is parked (scale 0) and x is driven.
pipeline._range: 0-5 (unipolar, DACRANGE code 0x0), biased at mid-range 2.5 V so the command has 2.5 V of headroom in BOTH directions without needing a bipolar range. 76 uV/LSB over the 5 V span -- 2x finer than +-5 would give, since the whole 16 bits now cover 5 V instead of 10. The 2.4..2.6 V sweep is ~2600 codes, plenty of resolution and nowhere near either rail.
pipeline._avss_note: AVSS MUST BE -12 V (NOT grounded) on this rig: the steering configs auto-range to +-10 so the mirror can be driven negative on an impact, and the supply is shared. That means this 0-5 sweep also runs with a negative AVSS, which is OUTSIDE the condition SLASEH2A 7.5 characterizes the unipolar figures at (TUE +-0.07 %FSR, offset, zero-code 0.15 %FSR are given at AVSS = 0 V; the -21.5 V <= AVSS < 0 rows are the bipolar ones). It is inside Recommended Operating Conditions (7.3: AVDD 4.5..41.5, AVSS -21.5..0, AVDD-AVSS 4.5..43) and the bipolar TUE at negative AVSS is tighter, so the part is likely fine -- but the bode measures the plant THROUGH this converter, so if absolute gain accuracy ever looks suspect, this is one thing that is not datasheet-guaranteed.
pipeline._footroom_note: The 1.25-1.5 V output headroom/footroom figure does NOT set a floor here: SLASEH2A 7.5 conditions it on -10 mA <= load <= 10 mA (1.25 V) or +-15 mA (1.5 V). Unloaded -- the EC table's own condition, and near enough true when driving an amplifier input -- zero code sits within the 0.15 %FSR zero-code error, about 7.5 mV of ground on a 5 V range. Only if the FSM driver actually pulls ~10 mA AND the output must reach 0 V under that load does a negative AVSS buy anything, and then it costs the characterized condition above.
pipeline._scale_sign: x keeps the NEGATIVE sign the piplate config used (was -2, now -1.0). That inversion is a property of the optical/mechanical path, not of the converter, so it carries over even though the magnitude does not. It is what made Kx come out sign-positive. If the push test now says otherwise, fix it HERE and re-run -- do not fix it by flipping the sign of K.

params._no_range_max: auto-ranging deliberately NOT enabled for a sweep. A mid-sweep range change would glitch the output for a frame and step the quantization, both of which land straight in the lock-in as a bogus data point. The sweep never leaves 2.4..2.6 V anyway, deep inside 0-5. Note the STEERING configs DO auto-range (range_max +-10) -- the bode measures the plant at a fixed 0-5 range and fixed 76 uV/LSB on purpose, so K and tau are not entangled with a range change.
params._verify: off in a swept/timed run: verify turns each write into 3 frames (write, read-command, NOP) plus a non-posted status read per bit. Use it in a bench smoke config, not here.
params._skip_unchanged: still worth having, but expect it to skip far LESS than on the BRIDGEplate: at 153 uV/LSB a swept sine changes the code almost every iteration, where 1 mV codes often repeated. Costs ~6.4 us/frame, against a ~264 us loop period.
params._sync_update: left off. Only ONE channel is driven in this sweep, so there is no inter-channel skew to remove and sync_update would just add a SOFT-LDAC frame per iteration.
